payload.title: How to Get Married in Costa Rica Step by Step
payload.excerpt: Costa Rica is on your shortlist, and before you choose a coast or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? In most cases, yes: Australia generally recognises a marriage that was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
key_takeaways: Two Australians can marry legally in Costa Rica, either before the Registro Civil or before a Costa Rican notary who declares the marriage to the Registro Civil online.
For the Registro Civil, each of you brings a valid passport plus a birth certificate and a civil status certificate, both apostilled and officially translated into Spanish.
The Registro Civil route starts with both of you lodging the request together in person, with the ceremony on average 4 to 6 months later, depending on the diary.
Registration takes 25 working days when either spouse is foreign, so build that wait into the time you need before the certificate can be apostilled for home.

faq.q: Is a Costa Rica marriage recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia, and your Costa Rican certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage.

faq.q: Who can legally marry us in Costa Rica?
faq.a: The Registro Civil celebrates civil marriages by appointment at its central and regional offices. Costa Rican notaries also celebrate marriages and declare them to the Registro Civil online.

faq.q: Do we need our own witnesses?
faq.a: Yes. You name two witnesses in the Registro Civil request, and both attend on the day, are sworn in, and must know you are free to marry. If you marry before a notary, ask how many witnesses the notary needs.

faq.q: Do our documents need to be translated into Spanish?
faq.a: Yes. Your apostilled birth certificate and civil status certificate each need an official Spanish translation. Official translators are found through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website, and the translation needs no further authentication.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in Costa Rica?
faq.a: There is no charge for the registry service of celebrating a civil marriage before the Registro Civil. You pay to publish the notice in La Gaceta, and a fee applies to apostilling your Australian documents. Ask any notary and official translator for their fees in writing before you commit.
